correctness_confidence.basis: I re-derived by hand the three-vertex decomposition of Thm 4 (vertices A, B, C, weights, matrix forms vs Lemma 2/3), the phase-independence of pure-output entropy e(p), the upper/lower bounds in Thm 1, and the arithmetic of Prop 12 (reversed parameters, J'(1/2)=0.1 ln(2^6 3^9/7^7)>0). No error found. Correctness still rests on the external Lemma 2 (Tang et al.; OpenAI note), which I did not verify.

rigor.basis: Scope, antecedents and non-claims are stated explicitly; boundary cases (zero row mass, u=0, endpoints) are treated; numerical results are labelled as non-certified. Some proofs are terse (Thm 6 complement step, Thm 9 covariance averaging, Thm 10 closure/continuity, 'maximum at p=1/2' in Cor 11) and would need expansion for a referee to check line by line.

novelty.basis: The new step is a third vertex (via strong subadditivity/Lemma 3) extending the Tang et al./OpenAI thermal-boundary inequality to the full Davies interior, plus the reverse-channel closure for simulation. The state/channel correspondence, complement duality and convex-roof geometry are explicitly antecedent. I did not search the literature, so priority is unchecked; the increment is real but technical and modest.

significance.basis: Gives additivity of Holevo information and a scalar capacity formula for all qubit Davies channels (including complements) and a parallel-simulation cost with a nonunital strict-separation example. Useful and well-scoped for a narrow family; original-channel simulation, adaptive cost, quantum and private capacity are left open, as the paper admits.

reproducibility.basis: Formulas are explicit and Prop 14 gives a discretization error bound. However, numerical tables and 16000/9000-instance audit claims depend on a supplement I could not see; scripts are said not to use certified interval arithmetic. I ran no code and recomputed no table value except the hand-checked Prop 12 numbers.

summary: The manuscript extends a block entropy inequality (external triangular lemma of Tang et al./OpenAI) from the thermal boundary lambda^2=k to the whole qubit Davies region by adding a third vertex from strong subadditivity, and derives from it unrestricted Holevo additivity and a scalar convex-envelope formula for the classical capacity of Davies channels and their complements, a strong additivity of state formation cost on the Stinespring range, and a parallel-simulation cost for the complementary channel (with a nonunital example strictly above the Choi-state cost). In my reading the internal arguments I could check are sound and the claims are carefully scoped. The main caveats are dependence on an external, very recent triangular inequality I could not verify, terse proofs in several places, and numerical evidence I did not reproduce. Nothing I found invalidates a main result.
strengths: Three-vertex decomposition in Thm 4 checks out by hand: vertex matrices reproduce the stated row masses and off-diagonal K, and Lemma 2/3 give the required entropy terms.
Clear separation of antecedent results from new contributions; explicit non-claims (original-channel simulation, adaptive, quantum capacity, region lambda^2>k).
Strict separation example (Prop 12) is exact-arithmetic and its numbers (reversed parameters, derivative sign) are verified by me.
Honest disclosure of AI-assisted development, non-certified numerics and absence of human peer review.
weaknesses: Whole programme depends on Lemma 2, cited from two 2026 preprints/notes (arXiv:2609.28592v1 and an OpenAI repository note); I did not fetch or verify either.
Several proofs are sketches: complement case of Thm 6, covariance/averaging argument in Thm 9, continuity and boundary handling in Thm 10, and the claim that p=1/2 is the global maximizer in Cor 11.
Numerical tables and audit counts are not reproducible from the PDF alone and are not interval-certified.
Significance limited to a one-parameter-family of qubit channels; no treatment of the phase-covariant region lambda^2>k.
potential_errors: Prop 12 uses concavity of the reversed-parameter entropy e_p on an open interval around p=1/2 (via negative quadratic coefficient) to equate G with J(p); this passage is brief and the interval of validity is not stated explicitly.
Thm 10 equality rests on the reverse-channel construction W_p and on 'establishing' continuity/maximizer existence for G; boundary values t=0,1 and p=0,1 are handled by short remarks only.
Prop 14 Lipschitz constant degenerates as min v -> 0; the paper notes this and gives no finite-L bound there.
strong_novelty_candidates: Closure of the Davies family under the normalized reverse-channel construction (parameters (19)), enabling the strong formation additivity to be applied to the complementary-channel simulation task.
Extension of the thermal triangular entropy inequality to the interior lambda^2<k by a third vertex.
